intention: Every internal/ module that owns persistence gets its own Postgres schema, making the modular-monolith boundary visible in the database and checkable at sqlc codegen time.
request: schema per module for internal/ modules

decisions.decision: Additive migrations (CREATE SCHEMA + ALTER TABLE ... SET SCHEMA), not rewritten history
decisions.why: 4 new files vs ~25 edited; needs no db-reset; leaves charging's backfill migration working

decisions.decision: Every query is schema-qualified
decisions.why: Forced, not chosen: sqlc fails codegen on a bare name once the table leaves public. Verified by repro.

decisions.decision: gen.go.rename with singularized keys keeps all 12 Go type names unchanged
decisions.why: Schema-qualifying renames every struct, churning ~144 call sites. Wrong key form fails silently, exit 0.

decisions.decision: goose unchanged; shared public.goose_db_version kept; migration-guard NOT retired
decisions.why: Version collisions are independent of table schemas. Keeps the roadmap reset-free. Follow-up is backlog #23.

decisions.decision: telemetry.supercharger_sessions -> telemetry.supercharger_history
decisions.why: Supersedes D5. Two tables both named *_sessions was the owner's actual confusion; a fleet_ prefix leaves both called 'sessions'. _history not _snapshots because this table is upserted as Tesla settles fees, while vehicle_snapshots is append-only -- calling both 'snapshots' invites a double-counting query. Matches the dx/charging/history endpoint.

decisions.decision: charging.charge_sessions -> charging.supercharger_sessions
decisions.why: The old name over-claims: the table is a Supercharger-only dense mirror that originates no value, yet reads as all charging, and analytics treats it and manual_charge_entries as two separate watermark sources. Reuses the name D5a frees -- accepted hazard: 133 doc files and frozen archived specs still use it for telemetry's table. Supported by RM31 D8, which already chose 'Supercharger' vocabulary inside charging.

decisions.decision: Generated Go type names follow the tables; NOT frozen (opposite of D3)
decisions.why: The renames exist to remove stale vocabulary, so freezing Go names would half-fix the confusion in the most-read code. Consequence: SuperchargerSession moves telemetry->charging rather than being renamed. Verified safe -- charging never imports telemetry.SuperchargerSession, so the swap crosses no import edge.

decisions.decision: Tier 4 blocked; charging's cross-module backfill read is fixed under a separate ticket
decisions.why: Owner chose to fix the boundary violation outside RM39. Tier 4 breaks charging tests A1/A2 until it lands.

decisions.decision: Tier 3 orders its migration CREATE SCHEMA -> SET SCHEMA -> RENAME TO
decisions.why: Tier 3 runs before tier 4, so telemetry still holds public.supercharger_sessions; renaming charging's table first collides. Moving the schema first lets both coexist -- and frees D5b from the D6 block.

decisions.decision: The rename DELETEs the affected vehicle_metric_watermarks rows
decisions.why: Post-rename the CHECK set is byte-identical to the pre-20260828000001 set, when 'supercharger_sessions' meant telemetry's table -- same string, two meanings by era, and Recalculator keys its cursor on it. A missing row means epoch per the table's own contract, so deleting is self-healing. Data loss acceptable (MAG-31).

decisions.decision: Every tier must also schema-qualify the raw SQL in its _test.go files (new work-shape step 2b)
decisions.why: Tier 1 shipped with query.sql qualified and every Claude-runnable signal clean, yet 10 integration tests failed: sqlc never sees test SQL strings and go vet treats them as strings.

decisions.decision: Owner turned autopilot ON and authorized the assistant to run go test / make test directly, overriding CLAUDE.md's Test-Execution-Policy for this run
decisions.why: Owner's explicit instruction. Scope kept narrow by the leader: only the LEADER runs tests, with env -u DATABASE_URL so containers are used; db-reset and destructive ops stay owner-only.

decisions.decision: Tier 3's design gate will still stop for the owner; tier 2's will not
decisions.why: Tier 2 mirrors the tier-1 migration the owner already confirmed. Tier 3 renames tables, rewrites a CHECK and deletes watermark rows (D8) — a big decision by the owner's own standard.

decisions.decision: A test replaying a historic migration out of order gets a search_path on its own connection, never a migration edit
decisions.why: D1/D9 forbid editing historic migrations. Analytics' watermark replay test broke without it. Scoped to one test connection, public first. Tiers 3-4 must check for the same pattern.

decisions.decision: D9's grep pattern corrected to match table names, not an opening quote; tiers 3/4 re-measured
decisions.why: Quote-anchored, it missed backtick multi-line SQL: predicted 5 for analytics, real 18. Re-measured: charging 32 in 10 files, telemetry 41 in 7.

decisions.decision: Tier 3 design gate CONFIRMED: proceed with D5b/D5c renames as planned, and D8 deletes the watermark rows
decisions.why: Owner re-confirmed after the leader re-surfaced both the name-reuse hazard (133 doc files become era-ambiguous) and the deliberate data loss. Rejected: deferring the renames, and renaming to a never-used name.

decisions.decision: D8 CORRECTED: the watermark DELETE + CHECK rewrite leaves tier 3 for a new analytics-owned tier 3b (json id 6)
decisions.why: vehicle_metric_watermarks is analytics's table, moved in tier 2; charging writing it repeats D6's violation. Precedent: 20260828000001 lives in analytics' dir though RM31 triggered it.

decisions.decision: Tier 3 renames ALL FOUR objects: index, CHECK, primary key and unique constraint
decisions.why: The roadmap listed only the index and CHECK. A duplicate-key error would otherwise print charge_sessions_pkey against a table named supercharger_sessions.

decisions.decision: D9's work-shape step 2b must cover OTHER modules' _test.go files, not just the renamed module's
decisions.why: Tier 3 renamed charging's table and broke 2 analytics tests that seed it by bare name. A rename escapes the module sandbox; a schema move alone did not.

decisions.decision: A rename tier's completeness criterion is the CATALOG, never a hand-written object list
decisions.why: Tier 3 shipped, passed review and archived with 5 constraints still named charge_sessions_*. Postgres auto-names one CHECK per inline column constraint; those names exist only in the catalog, so no grep finds them.

decisions.decision: Owner reaffirmed autopilot ON and test authorization; the leader runs tests without asking again
decisions.why: Owner's explicit instruction, superseding D10's per-run framing. Destructive ops (db-reset, DROP on real data) stay owner-only.

decisions.decision: While Docker is down, the suite runs per DB-package on its own fresh local database, never one shared db
decisions.why: env -u DATABASE_URL forces testcontainers, which cannot start. One shared db hits the duplicate goose version 20260720000001 (backlog #23) and fails account.

decisions.decision: Tier 3b design gate CONFIRMED: DELETE the charge_sessions watermark rows, re-add the CHECK with the new vocabulary, rename the Go constant
decisions.why: Owner confirmed at the gate. Rejected: rename-in-place (a carried cursor can silently skip data if the mirror gapped) and deferring 3b until tier 4.

decisions.decision: Annotated tier 2's vocabulary statements in the LIVE analytics spec rather than rewriting them
decisions.why: Tier 3b's delta is behavior-only, so tier 2's literal list became the spec's only vocabulary — and it named a retired value. Tier 2's scoped claim is still true.

decisions.decision: Apply the 3 pending migrations to the real database BEFORE db-reset, instead of letting the reset apply them to an empty one
decisions.why: The reset would have destroyed the only chance to test RM39's central claim — that these migrations preserve existing data. Rejected: straight to reset, and migrate-up without reset.

decisions.decision: Gate G1 (make db-reset) WAIVED; a fresh magus database will be built before the prod deploy instead
decisions.why: D23 already proved RM39 on real data, so the wipe's only remaining cost was irreplaceable history: 174 snapshots since 2026-07-13 and 12 hand-entered charge rows.

gates.name: database reset for fresh test data
gates.why: The owner wants a clean database to start testing on fresh data (MAG-31). RM39 preserves every row by design (D1/D4 use catalog-only ALTER TABLE ... SET SCHEMA / RENAME TO), so a wipe cannot happen as a side effect and must be an explicit gate.
gates.placement_why: After tier 3b because tiers 1-3b are the unblocked run and tier 4 waits on the D6 boundary ticket. Also avoids re-establishing the Tesla connection twice.
post_steps: reconnect Tesla through cmd/web -- db-reset drops accounts and tesla_tokens
run the poller once, then verify the pages render
gates.leader_instruction: HALT after tier 3b is archived. Do NOT dispatch tier 4 until the owner confirms this gate is done or explicitly waives it. Never run make db-reset yourself.
gates.waived_why: Owner will create a fresh magus database before deploying to prod instead. The gate's purpose was met another way: D23's migrate-up proved RM39 on real data, so the wipe would have cost 174 vehicle_snapshots since 2026-07-13 and 12 hand-entered manual_charge_entries — neither recoverable — for an empty database RM39 no longer needs.
